_comment: What `fix.ts --selftest` must produce for actual-dirty.json — EXACTLY this, no more and no less.
Hand-written, for the reason manifest.json is (docs/34-gate-independence.md): a manifest generated
from the plan's own output would be a gate built from its subject, and the direction it would fail to
catch is the dangerous one. Ordinary drift here fails as MISSING (an op that stopped being emitted).
The load-bearing direction is EXTRA: an op that appears for a category this tool must never act on.
A row is `op <kind>: <subject>` or `excluded <category>: <subject>`, and therefore a SET — the two
findings on `caption/md/default` collapse to one row, as they do in manifest.json. `accounting` is what
pins the counts, so a lost finding cannot hide inside a shared row.
The 24 findings of the dirty fixture sort into 2 ops and 23 exclusions. The two ops ARE the safe
boundary: the drifted value of `neutral/900`, and the one raw literal whose planned variable is in the
file. Its twin at `/caption fills` is right below it in the excluded list, planned variable absent, and
the two rows sitting one above the other is the whole design of this tool in two lines.
expect: op rebind: widget · size=md, state=rest · / · fills
excluded binding-presence: widget · size=md, state=rest · /caption · fills
excluded binding-presence: widget · size=md, state=rest · /label · textStyle
excluded binding-presence: widget · size=md, state=rest · /caption · textStyle
excluded binding-target: widget · size=md, state=rest · /label · fills
excluded binding-target: widget · size=md, state=hover · / · strokeWeight
excluded contrast: light · text.primary on background.primary
excluded contrast: light · interactive.overlay.hover on background.primary
_values_comment: 26/255 as a double, three channels — the emitted `rgba(26,26,26,1)` decoded for `setValueForMode`,
which takes 0-1 channels. Pinned because an op that EXISTS but writes the wrong value passes the
by-name check: `expect` says a write happens, `values` says what lands.
_collateral_comment: Both light-mode contrast contracts are re-measured through `text.primary`, which aliases
